evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'might take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time.' — time framing present, promise of personalized estimate present, but no explicit wait for a yes; customer simply says 'Yes, that's fine' in response to the original opener, not a pause after the quid pro quo itself.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Summer), moving day (Wednesday the thirtieth), from-to route (13610 Cypress, north Houston Road storage to 13415 Blackbird Drive, SAS), approximate size (15x10 storage, 100% full from three-bedroom home) — all four covered.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Joanna jumps straight into logistics: 'just wanna ask if you have any important concerns' was asked pre-call, but the formal 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move' was not asked.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (storage and two-story home), floor/stories (ground floor storage, two-story home), number of rooms (three bedroom contents), walking distance (can park right in front storage, driveway/street at destination), additional stops (sister's house for washer/dryer), special considerations (100% full, deep freezer present, some fragile items probed). Seven core items all covered.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Joanna: 'Typically for a storage deci we might end up with about $40 to $50 do you think you would just fall within that range in terms of boxes, or do you think you have more?' — customer responds 'Probably more. I don't know.'
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Never offered. No version of 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'typically a storage this size usually takes five and a half to seven and a half hours... I'll just put it more on the seven and a half to eight and a half hour mark... estimated budget of $1,755 including the transportation fee.' — anchor range provided (5.5–8.5 hrs) and personalized to this specific three-bedroom storage with one stop.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full framing present: 'we do charge by the hour... $95 per hour per mover... $190 per hour... includes two men, truck, wrap, insurance, taxes, credit card fees... one time travel fee of $140... no hidden fees... two and a half hour minimum... fifteen minute intervals.' All fee transparency and commitment language covered upfront.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. After stating the $1,755 estimate, Joanna transitions directly to 'would you like your help for this move on Wednesday?' without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or holding silence for reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Joanna: 'on time guarantee if we run late, we provide discounts for your move again, no hidden fees' — discount terms are stated but vague on the mechanics (when discounting starts, how much).
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Joanna: 'no worries, damage coverage. Which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any accidental damages' — $2,000 coverage stated, no-deductible/no-fine-print framing not explicitly stated ('coverage' implies it but is not spelled out as 'no deductible, no fine print'), and built into the rate framing is present in the broader price explanation.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Joanna never asks a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' after the Two Promises section. She moves straight from damage coverage mention into the move details and then the ask.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Never asked. Joanna does not ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any variant. She moves directly from the estimate to the ask.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Never asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Joanna: 'would you like your help for this move on Wednesday?' — asked plainly, BUT immediately followed by an easy out: 'I'll go ahead and send everything in an email. Of course, if you're ready to go ahead with the booking, you can just respond to the email or give us a call' — this is a built-in out that softens the ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Never mentioned. No reference to rate lock, holding the price, or any time sensitivity on the quote.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Not confirmed at all. Customer declines to book ('I'm kind of shopping around... I'm not ready to book'). No booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, crew notes) are collected.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details efficiently, including storage fullness, special items, room count, parking, and a third stop, giving her a solid foundation for an accurate personalized estimate.
coaching_note: You skipped the three critical mid-call checkpoints — 'Their Agenda' (Section 2), final concerns check (Section 6), and the 'Does that feel fair?' silence hold (Section 4) — and gave the customer an easy out on the ask; these gaps cost engagement and the ability to surface and address objections before the handoff.
